claim_text: Outside parties got into My docomo and the Docomo online shop
summary: Docomo says it confirmed unauthorized access from outside to its online shop and My docomo on Nov 4, and gives the cause as unauthorized access from outside.
detail: This is the company's own notice. Jiji Press and Nippon TV, which are independent of each other and of Docomo, report the same.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Docomo's notice is a Tier 1 statement, and two independent outlets report it.

claim_text: Docomo shut both services down early on Nov 5
summary: Docomo says it stopped procedures on the online shop and My docomo at about 1:05 AM Japan time on Thursday Nov 5, after seeing the access on Nov 4.
detail: Nippon TV reports the same start of emergency maintenance, at around 1 a.m. on Nov 5.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The company's notice gives the time, and Nippon TV matches it.

claim_text: Customer information leaked, for up to about 300,000 lines
summary: Docomo says its investigation confirmed that some customer information leaked through the unauthorized access, up to about 300,000 cases.
detail: Jiji Press and Nippon TV both report up to around 300,000. Docomo says no new leak has been confirmed since the services were shut down.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Docomo's own notice, with two independent outlets matching the size.

claim_text: The exact count given at the press briefing: 294,839 lines
summary: ITmedia Mobile, CNET Japan and Cybersecurity.com, all reporting on Docomo's Nov 6 press briefing, say up to 294,839 lines were affected, including customers who had already cancelled; 204,157 of them are personal contracts.
detail: CNET Japan and Cybersecurity.com put the corporate share at 90,682, which matches the difference. Docomo's written notices give only 'up to about 300,000'.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Three independent outlets report the same figure from the company's briefing.

claim_text: Names, birth dates, contact details, ID-document numbers and contract details leaked
summary: Docomo lists, for every affected customer: name, date of birth and age; address, phone number and email; ID-document number; mobile number, contract start date, plan, options and discounts. It says My Number card information did not leak.
detail: Nippon TV and Jiji Press list names, addresses, birth dates, phone numbers and ID-document numbers.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Docomo's notice has the full list; the two outlets match the main items.

claim_text: For some customers, bank account details also leaked
summary: Docomo says that for some customers the data also included bank name, branch, account number and account holder, plus the details of legal or procedural representatives, workplace or company names, and child-support program information.
detail: Jiji Press reports bank account numbers and account holders' names were among the leaked data.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Docomo's notice lists these fields, and Jiji Press reports the bank details.

claim_text: Credit card data did not leak
summary: Jiji Press reports that no credit card information was compromised. CNET Japan and Cybersecurity.com say card numbers were masked, so they did not leak.
detail: The 6th notice does not mention card data.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Two independent Tier 2 outlets (Jiji Press, CNET Japan) and a third outlet report it from the company's briefing; Docomo's written notice does not mention card data.

claim_text: The attacker exploited how linked systems work together to pull data automatically
summary: ITmedia Mobile, CNET Japan and Cybersecurity.com, all reporting on Docomo's Nov 6 press briefing, say the attacker abused the way several of Docomo's systems are linked together to search for and collect customer data automatically.
detail: Cybersecurity.com adds that the attack started from the d account system and that two-step login and passkeys worked as designed; only that outlet reports those details. Docomo's written notices say only 'unauthorized access from outside'. A full root-cause report has not been published, so the exact way in is still open.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Three independent outlets give the same account from the company's briefing. The d-account detail rests on one outlet.

summary: Cybersecurity.com says the source of the attack has not been identified. No claim of responsibility and no named attacker turned up in the sources we read.
detail: This page does not name or guess at an attacker.
label: Not established

summary: Jiji Press reports Docomo's president said the company plans to pay compensation, with who gets it to be decided later. ITmedia Mobile, CNET Japan and Cybersecurity.com call it a goodwill payment under consideration.
detail: No amount or eligibility rules have been published in the sources we read.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Four outlets report a plan; the details are not set.

claim_text: As of Nov 26, My docomo is partly back, the online shop is still down
summary: Docomo's 7th notice (Nov 26): the My docomo apps and site work again apart from some procedures, but the online shop stays in emergency maintenance.
detail: From about 5:10 PM Japan time on Nov 22, data usage, charges, d points and mail settings are viewable again. The My docomo iOS app was in emergency maintenance from about 5:30 PM on Nov 18; the 7th notice says it can be used again from about 3:00 PM Japan time on Nov 26 ("My docomoアプリ（iOS版）をご利用いただけるようになりました"). Some procedures, such as ahamo plan changes and family-discount group changes, are still unavailable. The online shop is still in maintenance, and Docomo says it will announce the restart once decided.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The company's own notices state the current status; the 7th notice (Nov 26) is the newest. Nikkei independently reported the Nov 9 partial restart of My docomo with the shop still closed.

claim_text: The Nov 5 5G network outage was a separate problem, Docomo says
summary: Nippon TV reports a nationwide 5G SA disruption from about 11 a.m. on Nov 5 was caused by switch congestion, and Docomo found no sign of a cyberattack. Service returned at 1:20 a.m. on Nov 6.
detail: We keep this separate from the customer-data breach. The reported cause is the company's early finding.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet, relaying the company's statement.

claim_text: The ahamo site was paused as a precaution and reopened
summary: Docomo paused its ahamo sign-up site on Nov 6 (Nikkei: from about 5:30 PM) as a precaution, and reopened it on Nov 8 after confirming it was safe. No unauthorized access to ahamo was found.
detail: The ahamo site is not part of the confirmed intrusion.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Two independent outlets, Nikkei (Tier 2) and Cybersecurity.com (Tier 3), report the pause and the Nov 8 reopening; ITmedia Mobile reports the pause was precautionary with no unauthorized access found.

claim_text: A mass-access alert flagged the attack, which came from overseas IP addresses
summary: ITmedia Mobile and CNET Japan, on Docomo's Nov 6 briefing: an alert for a large volume of access flagged the case at about 10:30 AM Nov 4 (Japan time). The attack came from overseas IP addresses, so Docomo first blocked access from abroad.
detail: CNET Japan puts that block at about 2:30 PM. When that did not work, Docomo stopped My docomo and blocked specific attack routes, then briefly restarted the service. Hours later its systems flagged possible unauthorized access again, and it stopped My docomo and the online shop. Overseas IP addresses do not show where the attacker is.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Two independent outlets relay the same account from the company's briefing.
